title: John Armstrong to James Madison, coded postscript of 30 Aug 1808 (THE=972 code), Madison Papers LoC reel 10 frame 0521

documents.shelfmark: LoC Madison Papers reel 10 frame 0521 (mjm015002); Founders Online (postscript undeciphered)

plaintext.source: Founders Online prints the postscript undeciphered; the LoC copy has only a pencil 's' under 1116, an abandoned decode. Tomokiyo (Unsolved Historical Ciphers) gives a partial reading of about a third of the groups from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter.

transcription.source: Founders Online group list, collated by hand against the LoC image (mjm015002, Cloudflare-blocked to scripts)
transcription.notes: Measured from the PS string in decode972.py (--digits, --skip keeping the three PS lines); the last token is written [555=>1555]. Corrections to Founders: 970 -> 972 (second line), 1218 -> 1216 (last line). The manuscript's final 555 (= re) is read as a dropped digit for 1555 (= man).

system.summary: Numerical word-and-syllable code (the = 972) of about 1,600 groups, alphabetical within runs, used for passages inside clear English.
system.sibling_key: The same THE=972 code in Armstrong's 1806-07 despatches, pencil-decoded by the State Department clerk on NARA M34 roll 13; used as the main key source.
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the postscript; about 580 groups of the code were reconstructed (pairs.txt, decode972.py table). Several groups share a syllable (1046, 1048, 1050 fi), recorded as homophones. The 20 Feb 1808 letter in the same folder is a different code and is not a document of this profile.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter (about a third of the postscript groups; code972_partial.json, 227 entries). No full reading of the postscript found in archive, print or online.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. The LoC image, blocked to scripts, was collated by hand; the NOTES do not say by whom.

solution.what: Took the 49-group postscript from Founders Online.
Loaded Tomokiyo's 227-entry partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter as the base layer.
Fetched NARA M34 roll 13 frames and ranked them for pencil with pencil_score.py to find clerk-decoded despatches.
Read the clerk's pencil decodes over the October 1806 despatch (frames 0192-0201) into pairs.txt (584 lines, H/M graded) and merged them with the base table.
First reading took the subject as 'S.' = Skipwith with 1394 a null.
Filled 12 groups by context checked against their alphabetical slot (1394 ru, 1273 el, 250 ought, 148 consul, 130 America, 720 bir, 992 qua, 1048 fi, 1202 above, 1052 fit, 384 Ward, 1483 ish).
Read the 22 Feb 1808 private letter in the same code with the merged table; it reads with gaps and fixes ru, ish and Russia.
Re-fetched roll 13 through the NARA catalogue proxy; frame 0190 gives 1320 = like and other H pairs.
Collated the groups against the LoC manuscript image: two Founders errors corrected, final 555 identified as a slip for 1555 man.
Postscript read: Russel ought to be the consul ... like Warden an Irish[man]; 48 of 49 groups determined.
Paired control: the 15 Feb 1808 despatch in THE=972 reads (176 of 243 groups H/C) while the 20 Feb 1808 letter gives noise (92 of 369 hits), so the latter is a different code.
Adjudicated the AFIO 2025 solution of the 20 Feb 1808 letter against a shuffled-ciphertext control (adjudicate_feb20.py); it fits worse than the control.
Reran the pencil score over all 393 roll-13 frames; it does not locate the annotated frames beyond the first page of a decoded despatch.

Crawled Founders Online's Armstrong-Madison chain through the Wayback Machine (founders_crawl.py, fo/), Sept 1807 - Feb 1809 early-access and the 1804-1811 published volumes; counted code runs per document.

Found that roll 14 (naId 188671566, Jan 1808 - Sept 1810) was already on disk in img/ (665 frames); paged all frames at 12 per sheet (grids14/) and located the long code runs: 0024-25 (15 Feb 1808), 0029-34 (20/22 Feb), 0476-77, 0494, 0495 (20 Jan, 2 Feb, 17 Feb 1810, with pencil decodes), 0643-44 (copy of 5 Mar 1808). Short runs (13 Aug, 30 Aug, 25 Oct 1808) were not visible at that scale.

Checked the Founders group lists of 15 Feb, 22 Feb and 5 Mar 1808 against frames 0024-25, 0034 and 0643; recorded 21 corrections in fix972.json (e.g. 22 Feb 1436->1456, 723 1357 755 -> 723 1337 255; 5 Mar 7->417, 1155->1165, 1150/893->1251/895, 1801->1201).
Transcribed the three 1810 despatches to Robert Smith (20 Jan, 2 Feb, 17 Feb 1810) from roll 14 frames 0476-77, 0494, 0495 with the State Department pencil interlinear (transcripts14.txt).

15 Feb 1808 read with the table plus context: hand, alliance, against, Great Britain (pencil 'G.B.'), if, war, kind, pick pockets, blessings, diligence, driven (pencil), trial, abandon, doctrine, well, come to blows, settlement, western boundary (pencil 'Boundary'); 1105 = comma, 962 = full stop, 1104/897 = semicolon. 243 of 243 groups given a value.

22 Feb 1808 extended: Gustavus (946 as Gu by context), old course, completely, humiliation, Bonaparte disdain to wear the crown, whose wealth, colonies, ally/enemy, true policy, threshold, altogether, American interest, Darien, common defence, restricted to Cuba and Mexico, league, commenced by Cretet seconded by Fouché supported by Talleyrand. 380 of 387 given a value.

608 is u/v, not 'va' alone: Gusta-v-us, Fo-u-ch-é, excl-u-de, fra-u-d (17 Feb 1810 pencil 'fraud'), act-u-al-ly; 773 = ea (sp-ea-k, 5 Mar) so the first Bonaparte in 22 Feb (773) is a slip for 723 bo, written correctly four lines later.

5/9 Mar 1808 (Armstrong's 5 Mar note to Lafayette and Lafayette's Friday reply, plus 9 Mar): Champagny, the jurisdiction of the judicial department sent to the grand juge, little encouragement, transmitted to Talleyrand, had not the opportunity, tomorrow, perhaps, indulge, Cretet, obscure and a little contradictory, exception to the operation of the November decree. 385 of 408 given a value.

27/29 Dec 1807, 13 Aug, 25 Oct, 26 Mar, 31 May, 6 Jun 1808 decoded with the extended table; 1810 despatches read with their pencil decodes (turn, negociation, duke of Cadore; Mr Petry, convention, reciprocal advantage; to justify the violence already committed on our commerce ... neither hasty nor uncharitable ... force or fraud).

Conflicts kept open rather than forced: 1260 = dou (22 Feb 1808) vs chari (17 Feb 1810 triplicate); 720 = bir (PS inference) vs 'da' needed in bri-ga-n-?-ge (26 Mar 1808); 396 = while vs pencil 'which' (17 Feb 1810); 1415 = be (C) and ble (pencil 'blessings').

Measured per-despatch share with despatches.py (shares.txt): H/C-known 64-79%; with M, inferred and this session's 160 additions: 15 Feb 100%, 22 Feb 98.2%, 5 Mar 94.4%, 27 Dec 89.3%, 13 Aug 92.6%, 25 Oct 90.9%, 1810 three 100%. The additions are context inferences ('?') checked against slot order, not independent confirmations.

The 1804-1807 despatches are printed decoded (italics) in the published Secretary of State Series from clerks' decodes or the editors' partial key; no group lists, so they were inventoried but not re-read group by group.

Located the remaining manuscripts at full resolution: roll 13 frames 0377 (15 Nov 1807 triplicate) and 0390-0391 (27/29 Dec 1807); roll 14 frames 0039-0040 (the original 5/9 Mar 1808), 0053, 0083, 0086, 0120, 0132-0133 (26 Mar - 25 Oct 1808), using the dated heads of every roll-14 frame (heads14/).

Read the State Department clerk's pencil interlinear decodes on those frames (pencil.tsv, about 150 values), e.g. 910 go, 240 master, 276 private, 152 council, 120 Wednesday, 1259 done, 206 journ, 733 bur, 977/437 scr-aw, 573/809/180/1229 most af-fection-ate, 1209 agent, 875/815 ret-ain.

Transcribed the manuscripts where Founders' group lists differ (transcripts14.txt): 27 Dec 1807 (9 misreadings, one dropped line), 5 Mar 1808 original, 6 Jun 1808 (Founders gives 3 of 10 groups, 1269 for 1209), 25 Oct 1808, 31 May 1808 (472 for 972), 13 Aug 1808 damaged groups (808, 1569).

Resolved conflicts by third occurrences: 946 = on (22 Feb MS has 914 gu); 396 = while (pencil twice, 25 Oct 1808); 1260 = dou (pencil 'doubt', 27 Dec 1807); 1415 kept two-valued (ble/be; Founders misreads 1405 as 1415 at least once); 720 left open (26 Mar digit 720 or 750).

Measured two ways per despatch (despatches.py: known = independently attested value; reads as sense = known or context-forced and fitting the English, minus sense972.json spans and weak additions). After: known 76-100 %, sense 95.2-100 % for 13 of 14 items; 26 Mar 1808 (5 groups) 80 %.
The 1804-07 printed decoded despatches were not re-read against roll-13 group lists in this session.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1581 tokens, 539 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.032 per letter; random keys -3.11 (z 11.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.243 (mean -2.254, z 18.1); annealer on the real text -2.233. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): copied the code groups from the PS string in decode972.py to texts/ps30aug1808_transcription.txt; saved the decode972.py ps output with the connected reading from NOTES.md as texts/ps30aug1808_decryption.md; key files code972_partial.json, pairs.txt, additions972.tsv.

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): the decryption file's connected reading is hyphenated syllable groups plus a code block (plain 0.333). Wrote texts/ps30aug1808_reading.md with the groups joined and the two doubtful points marked (qualifi[ed], Irish[?man]); plain 0.75, explicit 1.0. Keeps read.

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026) on texts/ps30aug1808_reading.md: the clear words of the postscript (P.S., and, much better, In a word, in general. Next to, but; the '|' runs of the transcription) left out; 32 code words, 2 holes (qualifi[ed], supplied ending, 1048 between 1046 fi and 1050 fi; Irish[?man], MS 555 read as 1555, slip rule not applicable to a rebuilt table). 0.957 (whole postscript) -> 0.938, under the bar: the postscript and the class move from read to read in part. fraction_read and fraction_coherent (groups) unchanged.

Coordinator's decision (16 Nov 2026): the four words on grade-M groups (148 consul, 130 America, 1202 above, 1052 fit; pairs.txt 'alpha+PS M', '?' in decode972.py ps) count as holes, sure words only. Postscript recount: 32 code words, 6 holes (those four, qualifi[ed], Irish[?man]): 0.938 -> 0.813. State and class read in part, unchanged from the first count.

Coordinator's second decision (16 Nov 2026): values graded I (slot-inferred, '*' in decode972.py ps) are not sure words. Russel (1273 el), ought (250), birth (720 bir) and Warden (384 Ward) become holes (qua and ish fall in words already holes; 1394 ru stays read, attested in three places). Postscript: 0.813 -> 0.688 (22 of 32). Class read in part unchanged.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The 1808 postscript (LoC Madison Papers) was read from a codebook rebuilt out of a State Department clerk's pencil decodes over Armstrong's 1806-07 despatches on NARA microfilm M34 roll 13, merged with Tomokiyo's partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter, with the remaining groups inferred from their alphabetical slot.
outcome.fraction_read_source: python despatches.py aug30 (2026-10-03): 48 of 48 groups given a value, 47 read as sense (555 emended to 1555); decode972.py ps gives the same 49-token count with the dropped-digit group.

gaps.item: PS 30 Aug 1808, qualifi[ed]: group 1048 sits between 1046 fi and 1050 fi, so the code gives fi and the ending -ed is supplied
gaps.detail: 1048 occurs once more (ver-i-fi(ed), 27 Dec 1807), with the same supplied ending and no pencil over it; nothing in the transcribed despatches settles whether the writer left -ed out or the group carries it

gaps.item: PS 30 Aug 1808, Russel (1273 el), ought (250), consul (148), American (130), birth (720 bir), above (1202), fitness (1052), Warden (384 Ward): values from the alphabetical slot and the sense only (grade M in pairs.txt for 148, 130, 1202, 1052; grade I for the others)

outcome.notes: 48 of 49 groups read as sense (fraction_coherent 48/49); the 49th is a probable slip. By distinct group in NOTES: 29 H/C (pencil decodes or Tomokiyo's known plaintext, including 1320 like), 12 slot-inferred, 555 emended; decode972.py marks ?/* but does not separate H from C, so grades are not counted. The first commit (2026-09-14) carries no model trailer; later ones Claude Fable 5.1. 2026-10-02: the table was extended (additions972.tsv, ~160 context values) and applied to 13 further despatches/runs of 1807-1810 (despatches.py, inventory.tsv); the profile outcome still describes the 30 Aug 1808 postscript. 2026-10-03: pencil decodes on roll 13/14 read; per-despatch known/sense shares in NOTES and shares.txt.

texts.label: Coded postscript, 30 Aug 1808
texts.summary: John Armstrong, US minister in France, tells Madison in a coded postscript that Russel (most probably Jonathan Russell) ought to be the consul, being American-born and better qualified than any other candidate, and that O'Mealy comes next but is, like Warden, an Irishman: the same animus against David Bailie Warden that led Armstrong to remove him in 1810.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1808, English, so the plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored the decryption file, whose connected reading keeps the syllable groups hyphenated (Ru-s-el, qua-li-fi(ed)) and a code block (plain 0.333, explicit 0.667). Reading written out as texts/ps30aug1808_reading.md, groups joined into words, the supplied ending qualifi[ed] and the emended last group Irish[?man] (manuscript 555 = re, read 1555 = man) marked: plain 0.75 (3/4), explicit 1.0 (4/4); the one sentence under the plain bar fails only on the name Russel and 'consul'. Every sentence holds. Keeps read.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026: read share over cipher words only 0.688: 22 of the 32 words written in code read. The clear words of the postscript (P.S., and, much better, In a word, in general. Next to, but) are left out. The ten holes: qualifi[ed] (group 1048 sits between 1046 fi and 1050 fi, so its slot gives fi and the ending is supplied; its only other use, ver-i-fi(ed) in the 27 Dec 1807 despatch, needs the same supplied ending); Irish[?man] (the manuscript writes 555 = re; 1555 = man is read as a dropped digit, but the code table is rebuilt here, so the one-digit-slip rule does not apply); and eight words whose groups are known only from their alphabetical slot and the sense, with no pencil decode, known plaintext or other transcribed occurrence: consul (148), American (130), above (1202), fitness (1052) (grade M) and Russel (1273 el), ought (250), birth (720 bir), Warden (384 Ward) (grade I): sure words only (coordinator's decisions, 16 Nov 2026). 1394 ru stays read (it reads ru in three independent places). Whole postscript, clear included, not the measure: 44 of 46 words (0.957), the figure recorded before.
